filler_text: A good day on the trail starts long before the trailhead. Pick gear that fits the trip you are actually taking, not the expedition you might take someday. Weight matters most on multi-day routes, where every extra ounce adds up over the miles, but comfort and durability matter on every hike. Try packs on with a realistic load, walk around the store in your boots for at least ten minutes, and check the temperature rating of a sleeping bag against the coldest night you expect. Layer clothing so you can adjust as the weather and your effort change. Carry enough water, know where you can refill it, and treat every source. Tell someone your plan and when you expect to be back. When you get home, dry your tent, clean your stove and restock your first aid kit so your kit is ready for the next adventure.
